subject: Request: red-team report + VPC scope details for private deployment
messages:
From: Peter Chen <peter.chen@stratushealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Security Contact <security@stratushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Requesting red-team report and VPC scope for our private deployment

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our security review for a potential private deployment, our InfoSec team needs the most recent red-team / penetration test report that covers customer-specific VPC deployments, plus a short write-up of the boundary and threat assumptions you use for private environments (networking, allowed management access, and persistence controls).

Specifically we need: 
- The latest final red-team / external pentest report (any redactions are fine)
- A 1-page summary of what boundary controls you assume for a customer-managed VPC vs. Redwood-managed infrastructure
- Confirmation whether credentialed tests were performed inside the tenant environment or only against public interfaces
- Current remediation status for any high/critical findings that could affect tenant isolation

Can you confirm ETA for these? We have a compliance gate with procurement the week after next.

Appreciate it,
Peter Chen
Senior Security Program Manager
Stratus Health

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Peter Chen <peter.chen@stratushealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Requesting red-team report and VPC scope for our private deployment

Peter —

Thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide the report and a boundary assumptions summary. Quick notes:
- The standard external pentest that Redwood commissions covers our hosted control plane and public-facing endpoints. For Private (VPC) deployments we have a scoped report that covers the integration points and any management-plane connectivity we configure.
- We can provide a red-team report redacted for other customers, plus a short technical memo that explains what we assume about customer-managed networks and the recommended hardening checklist.
- Mina (cc'd) will confirm whether credentialed tests were run in the Stratus-specific environment for the engagement you're referencing; if not, we can propose a scoped exercise.

I should be able to get a package (redacted report + 1-page boundary memo + current remediation summary) over to you by EOD Thursday (2026-02-12). Would that meet your procurement timeline?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Requesting red-team report and VPC scope for our private deployment

Team —

Quick status from Security/Assurance: the last external engagement (Nov 2025) included a scoped validation of private deployment controls, but only as a sample exercise against a mock tenant environment (non-customer data). It was credentialed for the management-plane interfaces we expose to customer VPCs (SSH jump host + API gateway auth flow) but we did not perform lateral-movement assessments inside production customer VPCs.

We do have: 
- redteam_report_v1.pdf (final, redacted) — includes findings categorized by risk and the remediation timeline for each item
- vpc_network_diagram.png — canonical diagram we share that explains traffic flows and control planes for Private deployments
- jira-7823-remediation-plan.docx — exported remediation plan we track in SUP-7823 (remediation for the two high findings flagged in the report)

High-level boundary assumptions to include in the memo: 
- Customer owns / isolates primary tenant VPC; Redwood requires a periodically-rotated service account and a locked-down management subnet for agent/ops access.
- Management plane connections are limited to specific CIDR ranges and deploy over mutual TLS; no persistent inbound access is allowed from Redwood to customer instances outside an approved jump host.
- We assume customers operate host-level logging/Sysmon; we ingest only aggregated telemetry and do not retain raw customer logs without explicit agreement.

I'll package the artifacts and draft the 1-page assumptions memo. Rishi, please add any technical clarifications on the management plane controls.

—Mina
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Requesting red-team report and VPC scope for our private deployment

Adding details for the memo:
- Management-plane access is mediated by a short-lived token broker; we rotate host keys quarterly and use ephemeral keys for agent bootstrap.
- The only inbound ports we open from Redwood-managed infrastructure into customer VPCs are our agent control port (TCP 49152) and the secure policy update channel (443). All access is tunneled over mTLS and mutually authenticated with customer-provided certs.
- For credentialed tests noted by Mina: the engagement used a bastion host provided in the mock tenant; no shared credentials were used across tenants.

Also flagging that SUP-7823 contains the remediation ETA for the two high findings (currently in progress; target close by 2026-03-01). I'll export the status snapshot for the memo.

-rishi
Senior Platform Security Engineer

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Peter Chen <peter.chen@stratushealth.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Requesting red-team report and VPC scope for our private deployment

Peter —

Attached: redteam_report_v1.pdf (redacted), vpc_network_diagram.png, jira-7823-remediation-plan.docx. 

Summary highlights included in the package: 
- The 2025 red-team engagement was conducted against our control plane and a mock tenant environment. Credentialed checks targeted management plane components (bastion + API auth); we did not run lateral-movement tests in customer production VPCs.
- Boundary memo (first page of the PDF) spells out assumptions about customer-managed networks, allowed management access, and telemetry collection.
- High findings in SUP-7823 are tracked publicly to your Security contact via the Jira link; current remediation ETA ~2026-03-01. 

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether Stratus would like Redwood to run a Stratus-scoped red-team exercise (we can provide SOW + timeline).
2) If you need signed attestation or a non-redacted report under NDA, we can facilitate that with our Assurance team.

If procurement needs anything else for the compliance gate, let me know and I can loop in our Legal / Assurance as needed.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redteam_report_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB), vpc_network_diagram.png (image/png, 340KB), jira-7823-remediation-plan.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 120KB)

From: Peter Chen <peter.chen@stratushealth.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Security Contact <security@stratushealth.com>, alerts@rdauditlabs.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Requesting red-team report and VPC scope for our private deployment

Vanessa —

Received, thank you. The artifacts look good at a glance. A couple quick follow-ups from our InfoSec reviewer: 
- Can you confirm whether the mock-tenant credentialed test included privilege escalation attempts that mirror real-world customer workloads? If so, please list the types of post-auth modules used.
- We'd like to schedule a scoped Stratus-specific validation. Please send a proposed SOW and estimate for a 2-week engagement (assume non-production fixtures).

I'll loop our procurement lead if we move forward with an SOW. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Peter
